- Code patterns, conventions, architecture, file paths, or project structure — these can be derived by reading the current project state.
- Git history, recent changes, or who-changed-what — `git log` / `git blame` are authoritative.
- Debugging solutions or fix recipes — the fix is in the code; the commit message has the context.
- Anything already documented in CLAUDE.md files.
- Ephemeral task details: in-progress work, temporary state, current conversation context.

Saving a memory is a two-step process:

**Step 1** — write the memory to its own file (e.g., `user_role.md`, `feedback_testing.md`) using this frontmatter format:

name: {{short-kebab-case-slug}}
description: {{one-line summary, used to decide relevance in future conversations, so be specific}}

---

{{memory content — for feedback/project types, structure as: rule/fact, then **Why:** and **How to apply:** lines. Link related memories with [[their-name]].}}

A memory that names a specific function, file, or flag is a claim that it existed *when the memory was written*. It may have been renamed, removed, or never merged. Before recommending it:

- Full spec: see `spec.md` in this folder. It is final; nobody can answer questions.
- File layout:
  - `server.mjs` (project root) — backend. Serves `GET /` from `public/index.html` and `GET /app.js` from `public/app.js`, both resolved relative to the folder of `server.mjs` (via `import.meta.url`), NOT the cwd.

  - `test/server.test.mjs` — backend tests. `test/app.test.mjs` — frontend tests (static HTML checks + app.js run against a small fake DOM/fetch, using node:vm or similar).
  - `package.json` — backend owns it: `{"type":"module","scripts":{"start":"node server.mjs","test":"node --test test/"}}`, no dependencies.
  - `README.md` — docs.
- Only Node.js built-ins. No npm install.
- Data file layout: backend's choice, documented in the backend note `.team/notes/api.md`.

- 2026-11-03 · backend · package.json test script is `node --test test/*.test.mjs`, not `node --test test/` · On Node v22 `node --test test/` fails with "Cannot find module .../test" (a directory argument is not expanded). The glob runs only `*.test.mjs` files, so helper modules in `test/` (helpers.mjs, app-fake-dom.mjs) are not run as tests. Name test files `*.test.mjs`.
- 2026-11-03 · backend · Data file validated strictly at startup (exact keys, valid fields, unique ids < nextId, no overlaps); anything else is "cannot read data file". Stricter reading of "not data in the layout this server writes".
# Backend API note (owner: backend, 2026-11-03)

## Pages
- `GET /` -> `public/index.html`, `Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8`.
- `GET /app.js` -> `public/app.js`, `Content-Type: text/javascript; charset=utf-8`.
- Both resolved from the folder of `server.mjs` (import.meta.url), read fresh on each
  request (so frontend edits show without restart). A missing file -> 500 `internal error`.
- Any other method on `/` or `/app.js` (HEAD included) -> 405.

## API (exactly as in spec.md)
- `GET /api/rooms` -> `{"rooms":["Aurora","Borealis","Cosmos"]}`
- `GET /api/bookings[?date=YYYY-MM-DD]` -> `{"bookings":[...]}` sorted date, start, room order.
- `POST /api/bookings` (Content-Type application/json) -> 201 booking
  `{"id":1,"room":"Aurora","title":"Standup","date":"2026-11-03","start":"09:00","end":"10:00"}`
- `DELETE /api/bookings/<id>` -> 204 empty body; 404 `booking not found`.
- Errors: `{"error":"<message>"}`, every JSON reply `application/json; charset=utf-8`.

## Data file layout (`DATA_FILE`, default `bookings.json`, relative to cwd)
```json
{
  "nextId": 3,
  "bookings": [
    {"id": 1, "room": "Aurora", "title": "Standup", "date": "2026-11-03", "start": "09:00", "end": "10:00"}
  ]
}
```
Validated strictly at startup (anything else -> `cannot read data file <name>`, exit 1):
- valid UTF-8 (no BOM), JSON object with exactly the keys `nextId` and `bookings`;
- `nextId` a safe integer >= 1; `bookings` an array;
- each booking has exactly the six keys, `id` a positive safe integer < `nextId`, unique;
  `room`/`title`/`date`/`start`/`end` valid per the Booking rules, `title` already trimmed,
  `end` > `start`, and no two bookings of the same room and date overlap.
- Written (temp file `<DATA_FILE>.tmp-<pid>` in the same folder, then rename) only on a
  successful POST/DELETE, before the reply. Folders are never created.
# Page (frontend, 2026-11-03)

Files
- `public/index.html` — static page, no inline script, no options/room names. Served by backend at `GET /`.
- `public/app.js` — classic script (IIFE), served at `GET /app.js`. Loaded by `<script src="/app.js"></script>` as last body element.
- `test/app.test.mjs` + `test/app-fake-dom.mjs` — static HTML checks and vm-run behaviour tests against a Proxy-guarded fake DOM/fetch (only the spec's allowed browser APIs are reachable).

Element ids
- Form `#booking-form` (novalidate): `#room` (select), `#title`, `#date`, `#start`, `#end`, `#book` (submit).
- Outside form: `#filter-date`, `#show-all`, `#booking-list` (ul), `#error` (p, role=alert, empty).

Requests made by app.js (path-only URLs)
- `GET /api/rooms` → expects `{rooms: [...]}`.
- `GET /api/bookings` or `/api/bookings?date=<value unchanged>` → expects `{bookings: [...]}`.
- `POST /api/bookings`, header exactly `Content-Type: application/json`, body `{room,title,date,start,end}` → 201.
- `DELETE /api/bookings/<id>` → 204 (body never read).
- Errors: shows body `error` string if present, else `Request failed.`; no reply / unparsable non-204 body → `Could not reach the server.`.

-# bench project
+# Room bookings
+
+A small meeting-room booking app. One Node.js server (`server.mjs`) serves a JSON
+API and a browser page, and stores all bookings in a single JSON file. There are
+three fixed rooms: `Aurora`, `Borealis` and `Cosmos`.
+
+## Requirements
+
+- Node.js 22 or later.
+- No dependencies. The app uses only Node.js built-ins, so you don't need `npm install`.
+
+## Usage
+
+```sh
+npm start            # same as: node server.mjs
+```
+
+Then open <http://127.0.0.1:3000> in a browser. Use the page to book a room,
+list bookings (all of them, or one date with **Show date**), and cancel bookings.
+
+When the server is listening, it prints one line to stdout:
+
+```
+listening on http://127.0.0.1:3000
+```
+
+The server only ever writes that line to stdout. Errors go to stderr.
+
+### Environment variables
+
+| Variable    | Default         | Meaning |
+|-------------|-----------------|---------|
+| `PORT`      | `3000`          | Port to listen on. The server always binds to `127.0.0.1`. `PORT=0` lets the OS pick a free port, and the startup line shows which one. |
+| `DATA_FILE` | `bookings.json` | Path of the data file. A relative path is resolved against the current working directory, not the folder that holds `server.mjs`. |
+
+An unset or empty variable uses its default.
+
+```sh
+PORT=8080 DATA_FILE=/var/lib/rooms/bookings.json node server.mjs
+```
+
+### Startup errors
+
+At startup the server checks `PORT` first, then reads the data file, then starts
+listening. It writes one line to stderr and exits with code 1 when:
+
+- `PORT` is not made only of the digits 0-9, or is above 65535.
+- The port cannot be bound, for example because another process is using it.
+- The data file cannot be read for any reason other than "does not exist", or its
+  content is not valid data, for example an empty file or invalid JSON. In this
+  case the message is `cannot read data file <name>`, where `<name>` is
+  `DATA_FILE` exactly as you gave it.
+
+If the data file (or a folder on its path) does not exist, the server starts with
+no bookings.
+
+### Data file
+
+The data file is a JSON object with exactly two keys:
+
+```json
+{
+  "nextId": 2,
+  "bookings": [
+    {"id": 1, "room": "Aurora", "title": "Standup", "date": "2026-11-03", "start": "09:00", "end": "10:00"}
+  ]
+}
+```
+
+- `nextId` is the id the next booking will get, a whole number of at least 1. The
+  server keeps it in the file, so ids are never reused, even after deletes and restarts.
+- `bookings` is an array of bookings, each with exactly the six booking keys.
+
+The server checks the file strictly at startup. It exits with `cannot read data file <name>`

**Verdict: pass.** I checked every line of `spec.md` against the code and the running server and found no spec violations or crashes. `npm test` passes all 216 tests. Since nothing failed, I sent no fix lists to the builders.

**What I checked**
- **Startup:** I probed `PORT` with unset, "", "0", "00000", "+1", "65536", " 80", "80 ", "1e3", "٣", "-1", "0x10", "abc", a 20-digit value, and a port already in use. Each bad value gives exit 1 with one stderr line. `PORT` is checked before the data file is read.
- **Data file:** a directory, an empty file, invalid JSON, a BOM, `[]`, `null`, and a path under a regular file all give exactly `cannot read data file <name as given>` and exit 1. A missing file or missing folder starts with no bookings and creates nothing. stdout is only the listening line, showing the real port when `PORT=0`.
- **Routing (raw sockets):** `/API/rooms`, `/api/./rooms`, `/api/%62ookings`, `/api/bookings/`, `/api/bookings/1/`, `//`, `*` and an absolute-form target all give 404. HEAD, OPTIONS and POST on `/api/rooms`, and `GET /api/bookings/abc`, give 405. `DELETE` on `abc`, `01`, `0`, `%31` and `1?x` gives 404 `booking not found`.
- **`?date`:** `?date` and `?date=` give 400. With the parameter repeated, the first value wins. A percent-encoded date is decoded. `Date=` is ignored. 2000-02-29 is accepted; 2100-02-29, 2001-02-29, 1999-12-31 and 2100-01-01 are rejected.
- **POST rules:** 415 comes before 413. Content-Type with tabs, parameters and mixed case is accepted; `application/jsonx` and an empty header are rejected. 10000 bytes is accepted and 10001 is a 413, including a 2 MB body and a 1 MB chunked body, and the reply always arrives. A BOM gives 400. Invalid UTF-8 becomes U+FFFD. Titles: 80 code units after trim pass; 81, whitespace only, and 41 emoji (82 units) fail. Date, time and end-after-start bounds behave as specified. The 409 reports the earliest-starting overlap, and touching bookings are allowed.
- **Concurrency:** 20 overlapping POSTs sent at once gave one 201 and nineteen 409s; 20 non-overlapping ones got 20 distinct ids.
- **Saving and restarts:** the next id survives a restart. A POST or DELETE whose save fails gives 500 `internal error`, nothing changes (the next id included), and the server keeps running.
- **`app.js` and the page:**
  - It uses only the allowed browser APIs.
  - Stale list fetches are ignored with a sequence counter.
  - `Book` and `Cancel` are re-enabled as soon as the request settles.
  - A 204 body is never read, and a 204 to a GET counts as an error status.
  - A non-204 reply whose body won't parse counts as no reply.
  - Neither `public/index.html` nor `app.js` contains `http://` or `https://`.
  - The page has no `<option>` elements and no room names, and the script is the last element in `<body>`.

**Test I added**
- A test for the "any other unexpected failure gives 500" line, which had none. It runs a copy of `server.mjs` that has no `public/` folder, so serving `/` and `/app.js` fails. It checks for 500 `internal error` with the JSON content type, that the server keeps running and still serves `/api/rooms`, and that stdout is still only the listening line.
- To make that possible, `start()` in `test/helpers.mjs` now takes an optional `script` path.
- The reviewer (Sonnet) graded the added test code 9/10, a pass. Its one optional suggestion was to split the two page routes into separate tests.

**Optional findings (no change needed)**
- In `test/server.test.mjs`, the "pages" tests skip themselves if a page file is missing. The files exist now, but a deleted page would show up as a skipped test rather than a failure.
- A data-file path under a regular file (`ENOTDIR`) is treated as unreadable, giving exit 1. The spec only calls `ENOENT` "no bookings yet", so this is the stricter and correct reading.
- The server validates the data file strictly at startup (exact keys, valid fields, `nextId` above every id, no overlaps), as recorded in `decisions.md`.
- HEAD replies are 405 with no body, because Node strips bodies from HEAD replies. That is allowed.
